chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hazza', from Abu Usama, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Mosque of Kufa is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. A thousand and seventy prophets prayed in it, and its right flank is mercy and its left flank is disliked. In it is the staff of Moses, and the gourd plant, and the ring of Solomon, and from it burst forth the oven, and the ship was moored, and it is the hub of Babylon and a gathering of the prophets (peace be upon them).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance and merit of the Grand Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the cosmological significance of the Grand Mosque of Kufa, portraying it not merely as a local shrine but as a microcosm of Paradise and a convergence point for prophetic history. By associating it with miraculous artifacts like the Staff of Moses and the Seal of Solomon, the text elevates its status as a sacred axis connecting the divine with the earthly realm. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual hierarchy of places, where Kufa serves as a primary center of authority and piety.
